_meta.note: Own-words consensus from manufacturer installation instructions. sources_agreeing counts manufacturers (ASI Global and Global Partitions = one), excluding AMPCO, which is an extra source and not a brand we resell; manufacturers_counted lists who was counted per style. Not for publication as-is; no manufacturer text, drawings or exact figures on the pages.
facts_not_for_page: Floor anchors: about 2 in. minimum embedment (Bobrick, Bradley), 2-1/2 in. (Global steel), 3 in. drilled depth for AMPCO drop-in anchors.
Temporary panel support: 12 in. above floor in most guides; 14 in. ASI plastic; 13-1/2 or 15 in. Metpar.
Ceiling rods project about 2 to 2-1/2 in. below finished ceiling (ASI Global); Global steel keeps finished ceiling to bottom of steel within about 1 in.
Bobrick TB-32: ceiling structure must carry roughly 275-295 lb per compartment and resist door swing and impact; designed by architect or engineer.
Bradley: ceiling hung not recommended over 8 ft ceilings (product sheet); cross bracing standard at 9 ft ceilings and above.
Plastic: allow about 24 hours to acclimate (Bradley Bradmar).

steps.title: Check the site, the drawings and the delivery
steps.summary: Review the layout drawings, confirm the room matches them, count and inspect the parts, and confirm wall backing and a sound floor.

steps.title: Lay out the run
steps.summary: Mark the pilaster line from the back wall, the panel lines on the walls and the floor fixing points, all from the drawings.

steps.title: Fix the wall brackets
steps.summary: Fasten panel and pilaster wall brackets into the backing at the heights on the drawings.

steps.title: Set the floor fixings
steps.summary: Install floor anchors with brackets, clips or shoes, left loose or adjustable for now.

steps.title: Prepare the pilasters
steps.summary: Fit panel brackets and the leveling bolt; slide the shoe on and hold it up out of the way.

steps.title: Rest the panels in place
steps.summary: Stand each panel on a temporary support in its wall brackets without fastening it.

steps.title: Stand the pilasters
steps.summary: Set each pilaster on its floor fixing and engage the panel in its brackets.

steps.title: Plumb, level and fasten
steps.summary: Plumb and level the pilasters to each other, set the door openings, then fasten panels to pilasters, tighten floor fixings and fasten panels to the wall.

steps.title: Install the headrail
steps.summary: Run the headrail across the pilaster tops, fasten it to each pilaster and to the wall, with a return to the wall at an open end and joints over a pilaster.

steps.title: Secure the shoes
steps.summary: Drop the shoes to the floor and clip or screw them in place.

steps.title: Hang the doors
steps.summary: Fit hinges, hang doors, set each door's rest position, then fit latch, keeper, hook, bumper and pulls.

steps.title: Final checks and cleanup
steps.summary: Check door swing, latch and gaps, test emergency access, tighten everything, remove labels and film and clean with mild soap.

advice: The headrail gives the run its rigidity: fasten it to every pilaster and to the wall.
Level the pilaster tops to each other before fixing panels so the headrail sits flat.
A loose length of headrail across pilaster tops works as a leveling aid before anything is tightened (ASI Global, Metpar, Bobrick).
Floors slope to drains: take heights from the highest point of the floor.
safety: Confirm backing behind every wall and headrail bracket before drilling.
Keep panels on solid temporary supports until fastened; components are heavy.
Make sure the latch's emergency access works before handover.
differences: Headrail timing: always before doors; after all pilasters are fixed (Bobrick, Bradley, AAMCO, AMPCO), pilaster by pilaster as each is plumbed (ASI Global, Metpar), alternating with hanging one door at a time (Metpar plastic), or first of all with the posts (Scranton Eclipse).
Shoes: before the headrail (AAMCO, Bradley phenolic, Global steel), after it (Bradley steel, ASI plastic, Metpar, AMPCO), or last after the doors (Bobrick).
Panels all placed first (Bobrick, ASI Global, AAMCO, Metpar, AMPCO) vs. wall pilaster first then alternating panel and pilaster (Bradley) or compartment by compartment (Bobrick composite).
Floor fixing: a shoe or bracket screwed to the floor that the pilaster sits in (Bradley, ASI plastic) vs. L-brackets or studs with a leveling bolt (others).
Starting point: highest point of the floor (AMPCO, Bradley level line) vs. a wall (others).
Scranton Eclipse is a post-and-rail system: posts and headrail first, then panels, then doors; Scranton says it installs very differently from conventional partitions.

steps.title: Check the site, the drawings and the delivery
steps.summary: Review drawings, confirm the room matches, inspect parts, and confirm the floor is sound concrete that can take anchors and the walls have backing.

steps.title: Lay out the run
steps.summary: Mark the pilaster line, panel lines and each anchor point from the drawings.

steps.title: Set the floor anchors
steps.summary: Drill and set the anchors (threaded studs or bolts) with lower leveling nuts and washers.

steps.title: Fix the wall brackets
steps.summary: Fasten wall brackets into the backing at the drawing heights.

steps.title: Rest the panels in place
steps.summary: Stand panels on temporary supports in the wall brackets without fastening.

steps.title: Prepare the pilasters
steps.summary: Fit panel brackets and slide the shoe on, held up out of the way.

steps.title: Lower the pilasters onto the anchors
steps.summary: Set each pilaster on its anchor studs with the top nuts loose.

steps.title: Plumb, level and fasten
steps.summary: Level with the nuts, plumb both ways, set door openings, fasten panels to pilasters, tighten the anchors and fasten panels to the wall.

steps.title: Hang the doors
steps.summary: Fit hinges, hang doors, set rest position, fit latch, keeper and accessories.

steps.title: Secure the shoes
steps.summary: Drop the shoes over the anchors and clip or screw them on.

steps.title: Final checks and cleanup
steps.summary: Check doors, latches, emergency access and gaps; tighten and clean.

advice: With no headrail, each pilaster stands only on its floor anchors: anchors must be fully set in sound concrete and pilasters tightened plumb both ways before doors go on.
Set anchors to a common level line, or take heights from the highest point of the floor.
Very wide end pilasters may need an extra support bracket to the wall (Bobrick).
safety: Anchors must be properly set in concrete; other floor types need different anchors.
Make sure the latch's emergency access works before handover.
differences: Whole run then all doors (Bobrick, Global) vs. one compartment at a time including its door (Hadrian).
All anchors pre-leveled to one string line before any pilaster (Bobrick composite) vs. each pilaster leveled on its own nuts (Global, AMPCO).
Shoes dropped as each pilaster is tightened (Global) vs. at the end (Bobrick, AMPCO).

steps.title: Structure above the ceiling
steps.summary: Before the ceiling is finished, structural steel is installed above it by others, with hanging rods at each pilaster position.

steps.title: Check rods and backing
steps.summary: Confirm the rods are where the drawings show and project correctly below the ceiling, and that walls have backing.

steps.title: Lay out the run
steps.summary: Mark pilaster and panel lines, plumb down from the rods.

steps.title: Fix the wall brackets
steps.summary: Fasten wall brackets into the backing at the drawing heights.

steps.title: Rest the panels in place
steps.summary: Stand panels on temporary supports in the wall brackets without fastening.

steps.title: Prepare the pilasters
steps.summary: Fit panel brackets and slide the shoe over the top end, held in place.

steps.title: Hang the pilasters
steps.summary: Hang each pilaster on its rods on support nuts and washers, top nuts loose.

steps.title: Level, plumb and fasten
steps.summary: Line pilaster bottoms up with the panels, plumb, set door openings, fasten panels and tighten the nuts.

steps.title: Add bracing
steps.summary: Fit any cross bracing or back rail the system calls for.

steps.title: Seat the shoes
steps.summary: Push the shoes up to the ceiling and secure them.

steps.title: Fasten panels to the wall
steps.summary: Fasten panels to the wall brackets and remove the supports.

steps.title: Hang the doors and check
steps.summary: Hang doors, set rest position, fit hardware, check emergency access and clean.

advice: The overhead structure carries the whole compartment and door impact; it is designed and installed by others before the ceiling closes in.
Keep the hanging distance from steel to pilaster short and the rods tight; long drops sway.
If adequate ceiling structure can't be provided, use floor-anchored or overhead-braced instead (Bobrick).
The floor stays clear, so the ceiling layout and structure matter more than the floor.
safety: If the overhead structural support is missing or inadequate, stop and tell the contractor.
Don't rely on the ceiling finish or grid to carry partitions.
Make sure the latch's emergency access works before handover.
differences: Installer fits rods through the steel (Bobrick, Metpar) vs. rods already installed by others and only checked (ASI Global, AMPCO).
Extra stiffening: cross bracing on tall ceilings (Bradley), back support rail for plastic (Metpar); Bobrick and ASI rely on the structure alone.
Panels first (most) vs. wall pilaster first then alternating (Bradley).

steps.title: Check the site, the drawings and the delivery
steps.summary: Review drawings, confirm room dimensions and ceiling height, inspect parts, and confirm wall backing and structure above the ceiling at each pilaster.

steps.title: Lay out floor and ceiling
steps.summary: Mark pilaster and panel lines on the floor and transfer each pilaster position plumb to the ceiling.

steps.title: Fix the wall brackets
steps.summary: Fasten wall brackets into the backing at the drawing heights.

steps.title: Set floor and ceiling fixings
steps.summary: Install the floor fixings, then the ceiling fixings plumb above them.

steps.title: Prepare the pilasters
steps.summary: Fit panel brackets and slide shoes onto both ends, the top one held in place.

steps.title: Rest the panels in place
steps.summary: Stand panels on temporary supports in the wall brackets without fastening.

steps.title: Set the pilasters
steps.summary: Fit each pilaster between its floor and ceiling fixings and adjust its height, loose.

steps.title: Plumb and fasten
steps.summary: Plumb, set door openings, fasten panels to pilasters and tighten top and bottom fixings.

steps.title: Seat the shoes
steps.summary: Seat shoes at the ceiling and the floor and secure them.

steps.title: Fasten panels to the wall
steps.summary: Fasten panels to the wall brackets and remove the supports.

steps.title: Hang the doors and check
steps.summary: Hang doors, set rest position, fit hardware, check emergency access and clean.

advice: Pilasters are made to the ceiling height on the drawings; check the actual height at each pilaster before starting.
Ceiling fixings need structure above the ceiling, not just the ceiling finish.
Plumb from floor to ceiling fixing exactly; a pilaster fixed at both ends can't be corrected later.
safety: Confirm structure above the ceiling at every pilaster before drilling.
Tall pilasters are heavy and awkward: use more than one person.
Make sure the latch's emergency access works before handover.
differences: Ceiling point found by standing the pilaster in its fixed floor shoe (Bradley) vs. marked from the layout with plumb bob or laser (others).
Threaded rods into structure above the ceiling (Bobrick, ASI plastic) vs. L-brackets anchored to the ceiling (Bradley, Global steel, AMPCO).
Telescoping top section to suit ceiling height (Bradley steel) vs. pilasters cut to measured height (others).
No headrail, except Bobrick's extended-privacy system, which can carry one.

general_advice: Read the whole booklet and work from the manufacturer's layout drawings.
Check actual room dimensions and ceiling height against the drawings before drilling.
Unpack, count and inspect parts; report freight damage at once; don't start with parts missing.
Floors and walls clean, smooth and finished; remove debris and protruding fasteners.
Store panels and doors flat, never leaning; keep protective film on until the end.
Let plastic (HDPE) adjust to the room; install in a climate-controlled space out of direct sun.
Solid backing behind every wall bracket; partition makers don't supply it.
Pilasters plumb both ways and level with each other; adjust with leveling bolts or nuts, not by forcing panels.
Set door openings to the drawings, square and plumb, before final tightening.
Use brackets as drilling templates; drill blind pilot holes where screws must not show; back up material when drilling through.
Hang doors only once openings are right and pilasters (and any headrail) are fixed.
Set each door's rest position; accessible-stall doors close on their own.
Clean with mild soap and water only; no acid, tile or abrasive cleaners; warn other trades.
Leave care and warranty information with the owner; local code compliance is the installer's responsibility.
installed_by_others: Wall backing or blocking behind brackets
Structural steel above the ceiling, and often the hanging rods, for ceiling hung and floor to ceiling
Any lateral bracing the engineer specifies
safety_all_styles: Don't install without confirmed backing and structural support; for ceiling hung, stop and tell the contractor if the overhead steel isn't there.
Components are heavy; use more than one person and solid temporary supports.
Review the jobsite for hazards and report them to the superintendent.
Every latch's emergency-access feature must work before handover.
Not following the instructions can cause injury or damage and voids the warranty.
